question: Why is regular self-reflection important for nurses working in post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees promotion to senior nursing administrative positions
options.B: It replaces the need for formal clinical pharmacology training
options.C: It helps nurses recognize their personal biases and prevent them from affecting care
options.D: It ensures the nurse never experiences physical fatigue on duty

explanation: Checking in with our own feelings helps us separate personal beliefs from professional duty, keeping our care fair and respectful.

question: A clinic wants more young people to visit. Which change makes the clinic truly youth-friendly?

options.A: Requiring parental permission slips for every routine blood test
options.B: Charging standard adult consultation fees for all procedures
options.C: Scheduling clinic hours on Saturday mornings to avoid school conflicts
options.D: Placing waiting rooms right next to the adult geriatric ward

explanation: Brilliant! Fitting into a student's busy school week removes a huge barrier to getting care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h2)

question: Why are urine cultures a must-have when managing a complicated urinary tract infection?

options.A: Complicated infections involve tougher, varied bacteria that need specific, targeted drugs
options.B: Rapid dipstick tests are completely illegal to use in complicated hospital cases
options.C: Cultures prove to the hospital administration that the nurse followed proper protocol
options.D: Laboratories require a culture sample before they will dispense any antibiotic medication

explanation: Complicated UTIs can be stubborn and caused by unusual germs. A culture helps us find the exact right antibiotic so the patient heals faster.

question: Which biopsy tool uses a tiny round, cookie-cutter blade to take a full-depth core of skin?

options.A: Punch biopsy
options.B: Excisional biopsy
options.C: Incisional biopsy
options.D: Shave biopsy

explanation: Think of a punch biopsy like a tiny apple corer! It uses a small, hollow circular blade to get a clean sample going through all the skin layers.

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move.

question: What is the main difference between illness and disease?

options.A: Illness is how the person feels and experiences their sickness, while disease is the medical pathology
options.B: Illness can only be diagnosed with lab tests, while disease is purely psychological
options.C: Disease is a subjective feeling, whereas illness is an objective medical label
options.D: There is no practical difference between the two terms in nursing

explanation: Illness is subjective and personal, while disease is the clinical pathology diagnosed by a doctor. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why must a nurse keep a close eye on urine output for a patient recovering from a severe drug overdose?

options.A: To determine if the patient has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To check if the patient is producing enough digestive bile
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric intake required daily
options.D: To evaluate kidney function and detect potential organ stress

explanation: Drugs and toxins put a heavy workload on the kidneys. Tracking urine output tells us right away if the kidneys are holding up or taking strain.

question: What is the main difference between a standard IV infusion and a blood transfusion?

options.A: Transfusions never require a special intravenous line
options.B: Infusions are always given faster than blood transfusions
options.C: Infusions can only use blood products while transfusions use plain water
options.D: Infusions deliver fluids or medications while transfusions replace blood components

explanation: You've got this! Regular IV fluids give water, salts, or drugs, while blood transfusions specifically replace parts of the blood like red cells or plasma. Simple and clear!

question: What is usually the very first warning sign that a patient's intracranial pressure (ICP) is rising?

options.A: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.B: A complete loss of all deep tendon reflexes
options.C: A subtle change in the level of consciousness
options.D: A severe decrease in peripheral blood pressure

explanation: Before vitals change dramatically, patients usually get a bit confused, restless, or sleepier than usual when pressure starts building.

question: A nurse is counseling a couple on birth preparedness. Which action is most important for them to plan before the due date?

options.A: Purchasing infant formula for immediate feeding
options.B: Deciding the baby's future career path
options.C: Buying expensive nursery furniture for the baby
options.D: Arranging reliable transportation to the health facility

explanation: Transport is key! Knowing how and when to get to the clinic prevents dangerous delays when labor starts.

question: Why should you check a patient's normal bathroom habits before handing them a bedpan or urinal?

options.A: It proves whether the hospital kitchen is providing the right meals
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever needing a catheter later on
options.C: It helps match the intervention to the patient's habits and preserves dignity
options.D: It tells the doctor exactly when to discharge the patient home

explanation: Great nursing is all about respect and personal touch. Knowing when your patient usually goes helps you offer help at the right time, easing their anxiety and keeping their dignity intact.

question: Why do we run lab tests and checks for patients in the intensive care unit (ICU)?

options.A: To replace the standard physical assessment entirely
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays
options.C: To track how well current treatments are working
options.D: To shorten the nursing shift handover time

explanation: Think of lab tests and diagnostics as your patient's report card. They give us real-time clues to see if our care is helping or if things are taking a turn.

question: What do we call the tiny finger-like bits of the placenta that dip into the mother's blood to swap nutrients?

options.A: Umbilical rings
options.B: Amniotic folds
options.C: Chorionic villi
options.D: Decidua basalis

explanation: Great job! Chorionic villi are those lovely little finger-like projections that increase the surface area so the baby and mother can easily exchange nutrients and gases.

question: What is the main reason for putting a Plaster of Paris cast on a broken bone?

options.A: To immobilize the bone ends for proper healing
options.B: To dissolve small bone fragments inside the muscle
options.C: To increase local blood circulation to the tissue
options.D: To deliver topical antibiotics directly to the skin

explanation: Spot on! The cast holds the broken bone steady so it can fuse back together correctly without shifting.

question: What is a big plus of using a flexible fiberoptic scope instead of a rigid one in the clinic?

options.A: The patient can remain awake and talk while vocal cord movement is assessed.
options.B: It completely eliminates any risk of a patient gagging during the test.
options.C: It provides a wider surgical field for removing large vocal cord tumors.
options.D: It requires full general anesthesia to relax the throat muscles completely.

explanation: Exactly! Because the patient is awake, doctors can actually watch how the vocal cords move when they talk or breathe.

question: Why do we use air ambulances for patients in remote areas?

options.A: It bridges the gap to advanced medical facilities
options.B: It is always cheaper than ground ambulance transport
options.C: Patients prefer flying over riding in cars
options.D: Hospitals do not accept ground transfers

explanation: Spot on! When patients are far away from big hospitals, air transport moves them quickly so they can get the high-level care they desperately need.

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main duties when it comes to environmental health?

options.A: Paving dirt roads to prevent dust inhalation in villages
options.B: Manufacturing chemical disinfectants in pharmaceutical labs
options.C: Educating patients and communities on hygiene practices
options.D: Constructing modern sewage treatment plants for cities

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Teaching patients how to keep their homes and habits clean is a huge part of community health nursing.

question: What is the main goal of holding a team nursing conference at the start of a shift?

options.A: To conduct formal examinations for student nurses
options.B: To review patient assignments and plan the shift together
options.C: To discuss hospital financial budgets
options.D: To discipline workers who came late to work

explanation: You got it! The brief conference helps the team connect, share updates, and organize duties so everyone knows what to expect before hitting the floor.

question: When does a medication error cross the line from a civil mistake into criminal liability?

options.A: When the nurse's actions show reckless disregard for human life.
options.B: When the error results in an extended hospital stay.
options.C: When the patient complains loudly to the ward manager.
options.D: When the hospital management decides to issue a query.

explanation: Ordinary mistakes usually fall under civil negligence, but extreme recklessness that puts lives in grave danger crosses over into criminal territory.

question: How does long-term fear and stress affect a patient's physical healing?

options.A: It speeds up tissue repair and lowers blood glucose.
options.B: It has no measurable impact on physical recovery.
options.C: It impairs wound healing and suppresses the immune system.
options.D: It completely stops the need for pain medication.

explanation: You're correct! High stress hormones like cortisol hang around during prolonged fear, which slows down tissue repair and weakens immunity.

question: What does 'rational drug use' mean for a patient?

options.A: Every patient leaves the clinic with at least five different prescriptions
options.B: Patients receive the right drug, correct dose, and proper duration for their condition
options.C: Doctors prescribe the most expensive medication available on the market
options.D: Pharmacies clear out all their expiring stock within forty-eight hours

explanation: You got it! Rational use means matching the exact illness with a safe, cost-effective treatment without waste or misuse.

question: Why must a nurse instruct a patient to remove all metal jewelry and hairpins before a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: The scanner's suction will pull metal objects into the machine.
options.B: Metal interacts with the magnetic field to cause severe burns.
options.C: Metal objects cause artifacts that ruin the clarity of the images.
options.D: Metal pieces block the patient from breathing properly.

explanation: Dense metal creates bright streaks and shadowing on CT scans, known as artifacts, which can hide important details about bones and joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h3)

question: A patient has a complicated hernia that a local clinic cannot manage. Where should they be sent?

options.A: A community immunization desk
options.B: A traditional bone setter
options.C: A secondary health facility
options.D: A primary health post

explanation: Surgical procedures like hernia repairs that need admission to a hospital ward are managed at secondary health facilities like general hospitals.

question: Why is it important for a clinical nurse to know about health maintenance agencies?

options.A: Agency guidelines dictate daily hospital protocols and safety standards
options.B: Nurses must directly fund these large government organizations
options.C: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on individual patient tips
options.D: Clinical nurses are legally required to manage agency budgets

explanation: Spot on! The rules, safety protocols, and daily routines we follow in the wards come directly from these health agencies.

question: A postoperative patient has a urine output of 15 mL over the last hour. What does this finding most likely suggest?

options.A: An infection in the urinary bladder
options.B: Overhydration causing the kidneys to shut down
options.C: Inadequate organ perfusion from low blood volume
options.D: A normal reaction to pain medication wearing off

explanation: When blood volume drops, the body reduces blood flow to the kidneys, causing urine production to fall well below normal levels. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which chemical gets released when tissues get injured, causing local blood vessels to widen?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Histamine is the chemical alarm bell! When cells are damaged, histamine rushes out, widening blood vessels and letting fluids flood the area—giving us the classic signs of inflammation.

question: Which organ in the body is the main factory for producing most of our blood clotting factors?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Kidney
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The liver is a busy chemical plant! It produces almost all the important proteins needed for blood to clot properly.

question: What is the main cause of metabolic joint diseases?

options.A: Gradual loss of cartilage due to normal physical aging
options.B: Direct bacterial infection of the synovial fluid
options.C: Chemical imbalances and crystal deposits in the joints
options.D: Autoimmune attack triggered by environmental allergies

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen when internal chemical errors cause crystals to build up in the joints, setting off painful inflammation.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four required elements to prove malpractice?

options.A: Actual physical or financial damages suffered
options.B: Breach of the established standard of care
options.C: Guaranteed financial recovery for the patient's family
options.D: Direct connection between the breach and the injury

explanation: Correct! Financial payout is a possible result of a successful lawsuit, not a baseline legal requirement to prove malpractice occurred.

question: Why are doctors and nurses careful about giving strong pain relief right away to someone with undiagnosed, severe belly pain?

options.A: Analgesics always cure appendicitis without an operation
options.B: Patients with stomach pain cannot swallow pills
options.C: Pain medicines cause immediate kidney failure
options.D: It can mask important physical signs and delay necessary surgery

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Masking the pain can hide how the illness is progressing, making it tricky for surgeons to figure out what's really wrong inside.

question: What is polyspermy?

options.A: The rapid division of cells before implantation
options.B: The natural death of the oocyte inside the ovary
options.C: The fertilization of an oocyte by more than one sperm
options.D: The complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate

explanation: Polyspermy happens when multiple sperm enter an egg, which causes a dangerous overload of chromosomes that stops healthy development.

question: What is the legal implication if you forget to chart a nursing care entry?

options.A: The hospital automatically wins any civil lawsuit
options.B: The doctor takes full responsibility for the missing note
options.C: The care is legally presumed not to have been performed
options.D: The nurse receives a bonus for saving paper

explanation: That's right! In a court of law, if it isn't documented, it legally didn't happen. Always chart promptly!

question: Why are small fish eaten whole with their bones considered such a nutritional win?

options.A: They are completely free from any bacteria
options.B: They provide a good amount of calcium and phosphorus
options.C: They supply all daily carbohydrate requirements
options.D: They contain zero cholesterol and zero fats

explanation: Spot on! Crunching up those tiny, digestible bones is a wonderful way to boost your calcium and phosphorus intake for strong bones and teeth.

question: Why is proper labeling crucial when taking skin snips from different body parts of the same patient?

options.A: To speed up the microscope staining process safely
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of laboratory processing
options.C: To determine how much local anesthetic was injected
options.D: To track which anatomical site yielded the parasites

explanation: Spot on! Parasite concentration can differ across body sites, so knowing the exact spot helps doctors measure how heavy the infection is.

question: Why is palliative care ideally introduced before the very final days of a degenerative illness?

options.A: To allow a smooth transition and build relationships with the care team
options.B: To guarantee that the patient will regain full physical mobility
options.C: To speed up the natural progression of the genetic disorder
options.D: To eliminate the need for any medications or nursing oversight

explanation: Early introduction helps patients and families process difficult decisions and builds trust with the palliative team before a crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)

question: In the OLD CARTS pain assessment guide, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Clock time the injury happened
options.B: Character or quality of the pain
options.C: Patient's coping style
options.D: Clinical category of the pain

explanation: The 'C' asks 'What does it feel like?'—is it stabbing, aching, burning, or throbbing?

question: Which of the following bodily sensations is primarily processed by the insular lobe?

options.A: Taste and internal organ sensations
options.B: Long-term factual memory storage
options.C: Fine motor skills in the fingers
options.D: Visual tracking of moving objects

explanation: The insula integrates taste perception and awareness of internal body states, known as interoception. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h6)

question: Which of these items is NOT safe to use inside an oxygen tent?

options.A: Silicone pacifiers used to soothe an infant
options.B: Plastic washable containers for holding water
options.C: Woolen blankets that generate static electricity
options.D: Cotton hospital gowns worn by the young patient

explanation: Woolen blankets create static sparks from friction, which is a major danger around high oxygen levels. Stick to cotton or safe materials instead!

question: What is another common name for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Cerebral shunt
options.B: Spinal tap
options.C: Epidural injection
options.D: Bone marrow biopsy

explanation: A lumbar puncture is commonly referred to as a spinal tap because it involves accessing fluid from the spinal column. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h1)

question: What kind of diet is best for a patient recovering from enteric fever to protect their gut?

options.A: Soft, low-fiber diet
options.B: High-fiber whole grain diet
options.C: High-residue raw vegetable diet
options.D: Raw meat and dairy diet

explanation: Well done! A soft, low-fiber diet is gentle on the tummy and avoids irritating the healing intestinal walls.

question: During an antenatal visit, how can a nurse best check a pregnant woman's nutritional status?

options.A: Give her a printed diet sheet in English without asking about her background
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about her usual daily meals and check her weight trend
options.C: Assume she eats well because she looks healthy on the outside
options.D: Wait until after delivery to discuss what kind of food she ate at home

explanation: Chatting warmly about what she actually eats daily and watching her weight trends helps you spot any nutritional gaps early and support her.

question: Why is being an advocate so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to manage court cases for patients
options.B: Doctors refuse to speak with families directly
options.C: Vulnerable groups often lack the voice to demand necessary health services
options.D: Local government budgets can only be managed by nurses

explanation: Spot on. Many marginalized people face roadblocks to getting care, so nurses step up to speak out and protect their health rights.

question: What makes intravenous therapy risky regarding how fast drugs act?

options.A: The slow onset of therapeutic effects
options.B: Unpredictable absorption from the gut
options.C: Total immunity to local tissue irritation
options.D: The rapid irreversibility of drug action

explanation: You're doing great! Once a medicine goes straight into the vein, you cannot take it back out. That's why we always double-check our doses—reactions happen fast and are harder to reverse than oral pills.

question: Where does a non-competitive antagonist usually bind on a cell receptor?

options.A: Directly inside the active agonist binding groove
options.B: Freely inside the fluid portion of the blood plasma
options.C: On the outer nuclear membrane of the cell
options.D: At an allosteric site away from the active spot

explanation: Instead of fighting for the main entrance, a non-competitive antagonist sneaks around to a side entrance (allosteric site) and changes the whole shape of the receptor.

question: What is the primary job of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) in the body?

options.A: Regulating the baseline basal metabolic rate of body cells
options.B: Releasing emergency calcium from bones during muscle tetany
options.C: Triggering water reabsorption in the kidney collecting ducts
options.D: Lowering sudden spikes in blood glucose after carbohydrate intake

explanation: T3 and T4 act like your body's engine idle speed, controlling how fast your cells burn energy and use oxygen every day.

question: Why do nurses give anti-nausea (antiemetic) medications *before* chemotherapy starts, instead of waiting for nausea to begin?

options.A: Chemotherapy drugs lose their chemical potency if antiemetics are not circulating beforehand.
options.B: Patients will refuse their chemotherapy infusions entirely if they feel even a slight hint of nausea.
options.C: Proactive antiemetic dosing ensures the patient remains fast asleep throughout the entire procedure.
options.D: It is much easier to prevent nausea from developing than to stop it once it has already started.

explanation: You're totally right! Prevention is key here. Stopping nausea signals before they trigger makes treatment way more tolerable for the patient.

question: Which main artery supplies blood directly to the uterus?

options.A: Brachial artery
options.B: Uterine artery
options.C: Renal artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: The uterine artery, branching from the internal iliac artery, brings oxygen-rich blood directly to the uterine walls. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is local anesthetic WITHOUT epinephrine typically chosen for a skin snip?

options.A: Epinephrine causes severe systemic hypertension
options.B: Epinephrine instantly destroys the surgical scalpel blade
options.C: Local anesthetics cannot be mixed with epinephrine under any rule
options.D: Vasoconstriction can interfere with parasite emergence from the tissue

explanation: Exactly. We want blood vessels to stay open so the tiny live parasites can easily crawl out of the skin sample into our liquid solution.

question: Which of the following is a common physical complication of performing high-quality chest compressions?

options.A: Severe internal bleeding
options.B: Rupture of the liver
options.C: Puncture of both lungs
options.D: Rib or sternal fractures

explanation: Compressing the chest hard enough to circulate blood frequently causes fractured ribs, which is an accepted risk. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h7)

question: In a court of law, how is a patient's medical record treated?

options.A: As an optional personal diary
options.B: As a legally binding document
options.C: As temporary administrative notes
options.D: As a draft of medical opinions

explanation: That is right! Charts are legal evidence used to prove whether or not proper care was given.

question: Why do we usually avoid combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives right after childbirth?

options.A: They prevent the uterus from completing normal involution
options.B: They can decrease milk supply and increase blood clot risk
options.C: They cause permanent infertility in nursing mothers
options.D: They stop lochia discharge instantly

explanation: Estrogen can dry up breastmilk production and add to the already high risk of dangerous blood clots that new mothers face. Smart nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What is the age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

options.A: 5 to 12 years old
options.B: 18 to 25 years old
options.C: 10 to 19 years old
options.D: 13 to 30 years old

explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent bracket as spanning from age 10 through 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main job of surgical swabs during an operation?

options.A: Absorbing blood and clearing the surgical field
options.B: Administering liquid medications to organs
options.C: Suturing deep muscle layers together
options.D: Measuring the patient's blood loss volume

explanation: You'll see these in every theatre! Surgical swabs are simple textile tools used to soak up fluids so the surgeon can clearly see what they are doing.

question: Which of the following is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor?

options.A: Biological sex at birth
options.B: Family history of heart disease
options.C: Elevated blood pressure
options.D: Advanced chronological age

explanation: Blood pressure can be modified through diet, exercise, and medication, whereas age, sex, and genetics cannot be changed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h2)

question: On a baby's head, what is the area located between the bridge of the nose and the front soft spot called?

options.A: Face
options.B: Occiput
options.C: Brow
options.D: Vertex

explanation: You're doing great! The brow sits right above the eyes and nose. If a baby tries to be born brow-first, it makes for a tricky delivery because that part is quite wide.

question: Which serious condition is a major maternal complication directly linked to severe, uncontrolled blood loss?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Massive blood loss rapidly reduces circulating blood volume, leading directly to hypovolemic shock if not treated aggressively. Keep up the steady pace!

question: What happens if glucometer test strips are left open to air and moisture for too long?

options.A: The chemical reagents inside them get ruined
options.B: They turn into a liquid gel substance
options.C: They change color to bright neon green
options.D: They become completely sterile to touch

explanation: Test strips are delicate! Moisture and air mess up the sensitive chemicals inside, giving you false readings. Always snap that strip container lid tightly shut.

question: What is the teach-back method used for during patient education?

options.A: Writing prescription notes for the pharmacist
options.B: Asking the patient to explain the information back in their own words
options.C: Having the nurse read the textbook out loud to the patient
options.D: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize medical terminology

explanation: The teach-back method checks whether the patient truly understood the instructions by having them repeat the information. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using clot-busting (thrombolytic) therapy in an acute ischemic stroke?

options.A: To prevent future heart attacks from occurring
options.B: To dissolve the blood clot and restore blood flow
options.C: To lower systemic blood pressure instantly
options.D: To shrink swollen brain tissue caused by edema

explanation: You got it! Thrombolytic therapy breaks down the clot blocking the vessel, getting oxygen flowing back to starving brain cells quickly.

question: A 15-year-old girl is admitted to the clinic with severe birth complications from an early pregnancy. What should be the nurse's immediate priority?

options.A: Provide urgent medical stabilization while ensuring a safe, confidential environment
options.B: Focus entirely on billing procedures before initiating physical examinations
options.C: Scold the family in the waiting room for breaking child protection laws
options.D: Refuse to treat the patient until local police officers arrive at the bedside

explanation: You're a natural! A nurse's absolute first priority is always immediate clinical care and creating a safe, trustworthy space for a vulnerable patient.

question: When managing severe asphyxia, what oxygen concentration is typically given right at the start?

options.A: Twenty-one percent room air
options.B: One hundred percent oxygen
options.C: Seventy percent oxygen mix
options.D: Forty percent oxygen blend

explanation: We want to rush as much oxygen into starved tissues as fast as possible, so 100% oxygen is the go-to emergency choice.

question: Why is it so important for a patient to stay completely still during an MRI scan?

options.A: Shifting positions triggers an automatic safety alarm in the control room
options.B: Movement blurs the scan and ruins the quality of the pictures
options.C: Patient movement interferes with the electrical wiring of the hospital
options.D: Moving too fast can cause the machine's magnetic field to shut down

explanation: Spot on! Just like taking a photo with a phone camera, moving makes the image blurry and hard for doctors to read.

question: When does a polyvalent nurse need critical thinking the most?

options.A: When ordering food supplies for the hospital canteen
options.B: When organizing the staff holiday duty roster
options.C: When filing daily paperwork at the nurses' station
options.D: When analyzing sudden changes in a patient's condition

explanation: Exactly! Critical thinking helps you spot trouble early, figure out what's happening when a patient suddenly takes a turn for the worse, and act fast.

question: What hemoglobin value means a laboring woman has severe anaemia?

options.A: Between 10.0 and 10.9 g/dL
options.B: Below 9.0 g/dL
options.C: Below 12.0 g/dL
options.D: Below 7.0 g/dL

explanation: A reading under 7.0 g/dL is a red flag for severe anaemia that needs immediate medical action.

question: What is the medical reason for performing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhancement of fertility during childbearing years
options.B: Reduction of congenital reproductive abnormalities
options.C: Prevention of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: There is no medical justification for the procedure

explanation: You got this! FGM has zero health benefits. It's done purely for cultural or social reasons based on myths, not science. You're doing great!

question: Why is a delicate balance of hemostasis important for a patient?

options.A: It maintains the proper blood pH balance during heavy exercise
options.B: It controls the exact amount of iron absorbed from the diet
options.C: It prevents both uncontrolled bleeding and unwanted blood clots
options.D: It ensures the heart rate stays within a normal resting range

explanation: The body must carefully balance clotting so that injuries seal properly without forming dangerous blockages inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference in how drug treatment is chosen for type 1 versus type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Type 1 is managed strictly through lifestyle changes without drugs
options.B: Type 2 patients never need insulin under any clinical circumstances
options.C: Type 2 can only be treated with injectable non-insulin medications
options.D: Type 1 always requires insulin, while type 2 often starts with oral agents

explanation: Well done! Because type 1 diabetes means the body doesn't make insulin at all, replacement therapy is needed right from the start.

question: What is the most severe and dangerous complication linked specifically to Taenia solium?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Neurocysticercosis
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: Obstructive jaundice

explanation: Correct! When larval cysts find their way into the central nervous system, it causes neurocysticercosis, which frequently leads to seizures and neurological issues.

question: A doctor asks if a pregnant woman can safely take a certain antibiotic. What is your best first step as the nurse?

options.A: Gather details on the patient's exact gestational age and kidney function
options.B: Immediately tell the doctor that all antibiotics are dangerous in pregnancy
options.C: Refuse to answer because prescribing is outside the nursing scope
options.D: Look up the generic name in a pocket drug guide without asking further details

explanation: You got it! Patient details like pregnancy stage and kidney health completely change how a drug is used, so always gather background info first.

question: What is the correct chronological order of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Alarm, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Resistance, alarm, exhaustion
options.C: Exhaustion, resistance, alarm
options.D: Alarm, resistance, exhaustion

explanation: The body first experiences a sudden alarm, tries to resist the ongoing stress, and finally reaches exhaustion if the stress is too prolonged. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h2)

question: A family caregiver looks totally exhausted and says they can't handle daily wound care anymore. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell them to stop complaining because nursing is easy work
options.B: Report the caregiver to social services for neglect immediately
options.C: Ignore the comment and focus only on measuring the wound size
options.D: Acknowledge their fatigue, offer reassurance, and review support options

explanation: Well reasoned! Caregiver burnout is very real. Validating their feelings and helping them find support keeps both the caregiver and the patient safe and stable.

question: Why do we need a whole team of different specialists for cancer rehab?

options.A: The physical and emotional needs of survivors are too diverse for one discipline
options.B: It lowers the overall cost of hospital administration
options.C: Hospital rules require multiple signatures for every session
options.D: Doctors are no longer involved in direct patient care

explanation: Cancer touches every part of a person's life, so it takes a collaborative team of different experts to provide truly great care.

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method?

options.A: To fulfill strict insurance billing rules
options.B: To confirm whether the patient truly understands the instructions
options.C: To give the nurse a break from talking
options.D: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity

explanation: Correct! Asking them to explain it back in their own words is the best way to make sure they got the right message.

question: Why is it important to ask patients about herbal supplements during a medication review?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of traditional medicines
options.B: To replace all hospital pharmacies with local herb shops
options.C: To report illegal herbal sellers to the local police department
options.D: To check for hidden interactions with prescribed orthodox drugs

explanation: Herbal products can interact strongly with prescription medications, altering their effects or increasing toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h5)

question: A family member wants to help their sibling remember daily HIV medications. What is a great first step?

options.A: Take the medication alongside the patient every single time
options.B: Wait until the patient misses three doses before speaking
options.C: Hide the medications in the kitchen to maintain privacy
options.D: Set daily phone alarms together to signal pill times

explanation: Smart thinking! Setting reliable phone alarms together is a practical way to build a steady daily routine for taking meds on time.

question: What term describes the brain's amazing ability to reorganize and form new pathways after an injury?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Osmotic demyelination
options.C: Neuroplasticity
options.D: Cerebrovascular atrophy

explanation: Neuroplasticity means healthy parts of the brain can step up and learn to take over functions lost from damaged areas. The brain is truly resilient!

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because they saw dead worms in the toilet after starting their deworming pills. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop taking the medication immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to take a double dose to kill remaining live worms
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a normal expected result of the treatment
options.D: Tell the patient to report to the emergency room for a blood transfusion

explanation: Fantastic! Reassure them—seeing dead worms in the stool just means the medication is doing its exact job and clearing them out!

question: What makes foetal hemoglobin different from adult hemoglobin?

options.A: It is produced exclusively in the placenta
options.B: It has a higher affinity for oxygen
options.C: It carries carbon dioxide instead of oxygen
options.D: It breaks down much faster in cold temperatures

explanation: Foetal hemoglobin grabs onto oxygen much more tightly, enabling the baby to extract oxygen from maternal blood. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h5)

question: Your patient cannot lift their hips off the bed to get a bedpan underneath. What is the safest way to help them?

options.A: Raise the head of the bed to the high Fowler position before sliding the pan downward
options.B: Forcefully slide the standard bedpan underneath the patient using maximum pulling force
options.C: Leave the patient without a bedpan until a doctor writes a specific order to lift them
options.D: Roll the patient onto their side, place the bedpan against the buttocks, and roll them back

explanation: Never force equipment under a patient! Rolling them gently onto a properly placed pan protects their delicate skin from friction and painful shearing forces.

question: Why is the antenatal clinic card given to the pregnant woman to carry around herself?

options.A: Because clinics are not allowed to store paper records on site
options.B: To prove she has paid all her hospital bills in advance
options.C: To serve as a ticket for free meals at the hospital canteen
options.D: So any healthcare worker can review her history during an emergency

explanation: If an emergency happens away from her regular clinic, any nurse or doctor can instantly check her medical history right off her personal card!

question: What sensation should you warn a patient to expect when the barium liquid goes in?

options.A: Total numbness from the waist down to the toes
options.B: Heavy sleepiness and deep drowsiness
options.C: A sharp burning feeling across the skin of the belly
options.D: A strong urge to use the toilet and mild belly cramps

explanation: Filling the large intestine with fluid naturally creates pressure and triggers bowel contractions. Giving patients a heads-up helps ease their anxiety.

question: Which route of exposure is responsible for the highest number of accidental poisonings in young children?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Inhalation
options.C: Ingestion
options.D: Injection

explanation: Young children naturally explore their environment by placing objects and liquids into their mouths, making swallowing the leading exposure route. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: Why must nurses monitor mental status closely in a patient with advanced portal hypertension?

options.A: To evaluate how well oral pain medications are working
options.B: To catch early signs of hepatic encephalopathy caused by toxin buildup
options.C: To check if the patient is getting enough sleep at night
options.D: To determine if the patient is experiencing a sudden stroke

explanation: When blood bypasses the liver through detour vessels, toxins like ammonia aren't filtered out and reach the brain. Checking mental alertness helps us catch early signs of confusion (hepatic encephalopathy) right away!

question: A patient goes home after treatment for a bleeding gastric ulcer. Which symptom should they report to the nurse immediately?

options.A: Mild gas after eating vegetables
options.B: A slight increase in morning appetite
options.C: Passing dark, tarry stools
options.D: Occasional burping after drinking water

explanation: Well done! Black, tarry stools mean there is digested blood coming from higher up in the gut, which can be a sign of dangerous bleeding.

question: How does cigarette smoking harm a woman's chances of getting pregnant?

options.A: It accelerates the loss of eggs from the ovaries
options.B: It causes the uterine muscles to atrophy completely
options.C: It permanently seals the cervical opening shut
options.D: It stops the pituitary gland from making growth hormone

explanation: You got it! Harmful toxins in cigarette smoke damage ovarian follicles, causing them to burn out quicker than normal. Every question you practice builds your nursing intuition!

question: What sign of infection should a patient on chemo report right away?

options.A: A low-grade fever or chills
options.B: Dry skin on the hands
options.C: Mild fatigue after walking
options.D: Slight thinning of head hair

explanation: Spot on! Even a small fever is an emergency for a chemo patient because their immune system is too weak to fight germs easily.

question: Why are involuntary reflexes like coughing and vomiting important for survival?

options.A: They increase the amount of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: They cool down the body during a high fever
options.C: They protect the body from harmful substances and blockages
options.D: They help the digestive system absorb extra vitamins

explanation: These protective reflexes quickly expel irritants or foreign items from the airway and digestive tract to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder before a physical examination?

options.A: To collect a routine midstream urine sample automatically
options.B: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the assessment
options.C: To reduce the overall weight of the patient before weighing
options.D: To ensure patient comfort during abdominal palpation

explanation: An empty bladder prevents discomfort and pressure when the nurse presses on the lower abdomen. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to look at the whole picture—not just a single medical diagnosis—when caring for older adults?

options.A: Because doctors usually make mistakes when diagnosing elderly patients
options.B: Because patients only care about their emotional health
options.C: Because aging affects physical, mental, and social well-being simultaneously
options.D: Because chronic diseases disappear once the home environment is changed

explanation: You've got this! Older adults often face physical, emotional, and environmental challenges all at once. Looking at the big picture helps us give the best care possible.

question: Why do patients need a broad support network during rehabilitation?

options.A: Families prefer to shift all medical duties to non-governmental groups
options.B: Hospitals lack the space to house recovering patients for more than a week
options.C: Doctors cannot manage chronic conditions without government supervision
options.D: Recovery continues long after hospital discharge and requires help from many sources

explanation: Healing doesn't stop just because the patient goes home. Family, community, and healthcare teams all team up to keep the momentum going!

question: A patient is very anxious about tests for a suspected adrenal tumor. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to refuse all invasive tests until they feel calmer
options.B: Provide clear, simple explanations of the tests and offer emotional support
options.C: Administer a strong sedative without a doctor's prescription
options.D: Reassure the patient that adrenal tumors are never cancerous

explanation: You're a natural! Clear, compassionate communication and emotional support go a long way in calming patient fears and helping them through tests.

question: What is a heartbreaking result of unwanted pregnancies in places where safe care isn't available?

options.A: Guaranteed delivery of healthy twins
options.B: Automatic enrollment in advanced academic scholarships
options.C: Immediate maternal immunity against infectious diseases
options.D: Unsafe abortions leading to severe infection and bleeding

explanation: When women lack access to safe options, they often resort to dangerous procedures that cause terrible injuries and loss of life.

question: Which of these is a common everyday distraction during a home health visit?

options.A: Frequent interruptions from attending physicians
options.B: Mandatory shift-change meetings in the hallway
options.C: Strict hospital visiting hour regulations
options.D: Background noise from household sources and family members

explanation: Unlike quiet hospital wards, homes are full of life! TVs playing, pets barking, and family chatting can make focusing a bit tricky.

question: How does increased blood flow help an infected, swollen area under a poultice?

options.A: It dries out all body fluids completely
options.B: It cools down the fever instantly
options.C: It brings white blood cells to fight the infection
options.D: It stops the heart from pumping too fast

explanation: Extra blood circulation delivers necessary white blood cells and nutrients to heal inflamed or infected tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why is communication especially critical for the home health care team compared to a hospital staff?

options.A: Hospital staff do not communicate with each other during shifts
options.B: Team members work independently in scattered locations rather than in one building
options.C: Home health personnel rarely document patient progress in charts
options.D: Patients manage their own medications without professional input

explanation: Because home health workers operate separately in different homes, clear and timely communication is vital to keep everyone updated on patient status. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a very common complaint you will hear from patients who have anaemia?

options.A: Chronic fatigue and shortness of breath
options.B: Uncontrolled involuntary muscle twitching
options.C: Sudden inability to move the left arm
options.D: Severe pain in the lower right abdomen

explanation: When red blood cells are low, they carry less oxygen. This leaves the body tissues starving for oxygen, causing constant tiredness and breathlessness.

question: Why must you NEVER use a tongue depressor to check the throat of a child you suspect has acute epiglottitis?

options.A: It causes severe pain in the gums
options.B: It interferes with accurate pulse oximetry
options.C: It can trigger sudden total airway closure
options.D: It makes the fever spike higher immediately

explanation: Well done! Pressing down on an already swollen, angry epiglottis can cause sudden muscle spasms and completely block the child's airway. Safety first—leave it alone!

question: What is a major limitation of receiving care in a residential home?

options.A: Inability of nurses to administer any form of liquid medication
options.B: Strict regulations that forbid doctors from visiting private houses
options.C: Mandatory requirement for patients to cook their own hospital meals
options.D: Absence of 24-hour bedside monitoring equipment and immediate emergency teams

explanation: Homes do not possess the constant electronic monitoring and instant backup staff available in hospital units. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which test gives doctors the final, definitive confirmation that a patient has lung cancer?

options.A: Pulmonary function test
options.B: Tissue biopsy
options.C: Routine chest X-ray
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Spot on! Scans can strongly suggest cancer, but a pathologist needs to look at an actual tissue sample under a microscope to confirm it.

question: What is the right approach when counseling a PAC patient on family planning and contraception?

options.A: Withholding contraceptive information to encourage abstinence
options.B: Ensuring the advice is non-coercive and respects her personal choices
options.C: Choosing the most expensive birth control method for her automatically
options.D: Insisting that she accepts permanent sterilization before leaving

explanation: Contraceptive counseling should empower her with choices, never force or pressure her into a method she doesn't want.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual synthesis and production of breast milk?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Prolactin is secreted by the anterior pituitary gland to stimulate milk production in the alveoli. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h1)

question: A newborn is experiencing severe breathing trouble and low oxygen levels. What happens to the blood vessels in the baby's lungs as a result?

options.A: They stop pumping blood back to the right atrium
options.B: They stay constricted, keeping pulmonary resistance high
options.C: They dilate widely to let extra blood flow through
options.D: They turn into permanent fibrous ligaments right away

question: Why do some women who use diaphragms experience more frequent urinary tract infections (UTIs)?

options.A: The spermicide alters the normal bacterial balance inside the urinary bladder
options.B: The device prevents regular urination while it is worn during the day
options.C: The silicone material absorbs urine and introduces bacteria into the kidneys
options.D: The rim of the device can press against the urethra and block complete bladder emptying

explanation: The diaphragm rim can put slight pressure on the urethra, making it harder to empty the bladder completely and causing UTIs.

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time when someone has a bacterial STI?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory insurance claim covers the cost of the initial diagnostic workup
options.B: To speed up the metabolic clearance of the antibiotic through the kidneys
options.C: To prevent the patient from becoming immediately reinfected after finishing treatment
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant fungal strains in the community

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously stops the back-and-forth 'ping-pong' spread of the infection between couples.

question: What is the main job of the lactiferous sinuses when a mother is breastfeeding?

options.A: They produce the hormone prolactin for milk synthesis
options.B: They filter waste products out of the breast milk
options.C: They secrete lubricating oils to protect the areola
options.D: They temporarily store milk before it reaches the nipple

question: Who are considered primary gatekeepers of cultural norms in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: International donor agencies
options.B: Pharmaceutical sales representatives
options.C: Federal ministry accountants
options.D: Traditional and religious leaders

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold significant influence over community values and must be engaged for health programs to succeed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: Which lobe of the brain contains the primary visual cortex?

options.A: Parietal lobe
options.B: Frontal lobe
options.C: Occipital lobe
options.D: Temporal lobe

question: Which public health measure helps protect people from getting human papillomavirus (HPV)?

options.A: Surgical removal
options.B: Daily antibiotics
options.C: Vaccination
options.D: Vitamin C therapy

explanation: You got it! Vaccines are our best primary defense because they train the immune system to fight off viruses like HPV before exposure ever happens.

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a freely moving joint?

options.A: To lubricate the joint and nourish the cartilage
options.B: To produce new red blood cells for the joint space
options.C: To anchor skeletal muscles directly to the bone ends
options.D: To generate electrical impulses for joint movement

question: Which scenario is an example of natural passive immunity?

options.A: A patient recovering completely from a severe bout of malaria
options.B: A pregnant woman receiving a tetanus toxoid booster shot
options.C: An infant receiving protective antibodies through breast milk
options.D: A traveler receiving a shot of hepatitis B immunoglobulin

explanation: Passing antibodies from a mother to her baby via breast milk or the placenta is a natural way to provide temporary passive protection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) differ from the earlier selective health approaches?

options.A: They rely only on private hospitals instead of community clinics
options.B: They focus exclusively on curing adult heart disease in wealthy nations
options.C: They completely ignore maternal and child health in favor of space research
options.D: They return to a broader, more comprehensive vision of health linked to overall development

explanation: SDG 3 and related goals embrace a wide-ranging view of health and well-being, echoing the holistic spirit of the original Alma-Ata declaration. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: A nurse checks a patient's pedal pulses and finds the left pulse is strong while the right pulse cannot be felt at all. What is the most immediate clinical concern?

options.A: High blood pressure throughout the body
options.B: A potential blockage in the right leg artery
options.C: An allergic reaction to heart medication
options.D: A normal variation in elderly patients

explanation: An absent pulse on only one side strongly suggests local arterial occlusion or injury, requiring urgent follow-up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: A patient looks very anxious while preparing for a pelvic exam for lower belly pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Skip the speculum exam entirely and prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics without testing
options.B: Insist she lie back immediately to keep the clinic schedule running on time
options.C: Explain each step of the procedure calmly and reassure her about privacy and comfort
options.D: Ask a security guard to stand in the room until the examination is finished

explanation: As a nurse, your warmth and clear explanations help ease patient fears, build trust, and make the clinical exam go much smoother.

question: A community clinic wants to stop teenagers from dropping out of care. What should they do first?

options.A: Require formal written permission from local chiefs
options.B: Move the clinic to a remote location outside the city
options.C: Offer drop-in services and reduce long waiting times
options.D: Increase fees to cover new facility decorations

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down long delays and allowing flexible drop-in visits keeps young people engaged and willing to return.

question: Which nursing action is best for preventing constipation in an immobile bedbound patient?

options.A: Administering a strong daily enema before breakfast
options.B: Encouraging fluids, high-fiber foods, and passive or active movement
options.C: Telling the patient to hold bowel movements until evening
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to slow down digestion

question: How does the pressure for marriageability drive the continuation of FGM?

options.A: Grooms pay higher bride prices directly to local surgeons

options.D: Parents fear their daughters will face poverty and isolation without a husband

question: Why do nurses pinch the skin when giving a subcutaneous injection to a slim patient?

options.A: To squeeze out trapped air bubbles inside the syringe

question: When does emergency contraception work most effectively?

options.A: When taken as soon as possible after unprotected sex
options.B: When administered right before the start of a menstrual period
options.C: When combined with daily prenatal vitamin supplements
options.D: When swallowed exactly fourteen days after ovulation

explanation: Time is everything! Emergency pills work best when taken promptly before ovulation happens.

question: What is the term for a patient's right to make independent decisions about their own medical treatment?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Negligence
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Malpractice

explanation: Correct! Autonomy simply means self-rule—giving every competent patient the full right to make their own healthcare choices.

question: A client 4 weeks post-vasectomy asks if he can stop using condoms since he feels great. What is your best advice?

options.A: You can stop condoms now since four weeks is enough healing time
options.B: Continue using birth control until your semen analysis confirms zero sperm
options.C: Wait for one more week and then you can safely discard condoms
options.D: Stop using condoms only if you haven't experienced any swelling

explanation: Correct! Always remind clients to keep using backup contraception until a lab test officially confirms the semen is sperm-free.

question: Why is spotting a high-risk labour early on so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any postpartum medication
options.B: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient within one hour
options.C: It guarantees the mother will experience a painless delivery
options.D: It prevents small problems from turning into life-threatening emergencies

explanation: Spotting risks early is a superpower in nursing! It gives our team time to step in before a small issue turns into a major crisis.

question: What is a major danger of having bad sanitation and broken toilets in a school?

options.A: Rapid spread of infectious diseases like cholera
options.B: Immediate decline in mathematical reasoning skills
options.C: Permanent loss of hearing acuity in students
options.D: Sudden increase in genetic disorders among pupils

explanation: Correct! Dirty surroundings and unsafe water easily lead to water-borne illnesses and tummy infections among children.

question: What finding in a pregnant patient's urine points to prolonged vomiting and starvation?

options.A: Ketones
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: When the body can't keep food down, it starts burning its own fat for fuel. This breakdown leaves behind ketones in the urine—a classic sign of prolonged vomiting!

question: What does 'appropriate information' mean in the context of rational drug use?

options.A: Giving clear instructions to the patient on how to take the medicine
options.B: Reporting drug manufacturing errors directly to the national health ministry
options.C: Publishing treatment outcomes in international medical and nursing journals
options.D: Filing the patient medical folder in the correct hospital archive cabinet

explanation: Appropriate information ensures that patients understand how, when, and why to take their prescribed medications safely. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles and slowing down digestion in pregnancy?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone is the relaxing hormone that keeps the womb safe, but it also relaxes the bowel muscles, making digestion slower.

question: Which nursing instruction is most important for a patient with chronic venous insufficiency?

options.A: Restrict your daily water intake to stop leg swelling
options.B: Keep your legs elevated above heart level whenever you are resting
options.C: Avoid wearing compression stockings because they block blood flow
options.D: Apply hot water packs to your lower calves twice a day

explanation: Gravity is our enemy when veins are weak. Propping those legs up high helps gravity slide the blood smoothly back toward the heart instead of pooling in the ankles!

question: Which group of patients is most often affected by drug under-prescription?

options.A: Children admitted for acute infectious diseases
options.B: Young healthy adults visiting emergency rooms
options.C: Athletes recovering from orthopedic surgeries
options.D: Older adults and those with multiple chronic illnesses

explanation: Spot on! Older patients and those with complex health issues often miss out on necessary care because healthcare providers worry too much about drug interactions.

question: A patient's IVP report notes a 'filling defect' in the right ureter. What condition is the radiologist most likely describing?

options.A: An abnormal mass or kidney stone taking up space
options.B: An area where the contrast dye failed to reach at all
options.C: A normal pocket of air trapped inside the bladder
options.D: A normal variation in the size of the right kidney

question: Which of these is an unhelpful thing to say to someone who is grieving?

options.A: Time heals all wounds.
options.B: I am here for you.
options.C: Would you like to talk about her?
options.D: It is okay to feel angry.

explanation: Clichés like 'time heals all wounds' tend to dismiss personal pain and shut down honest conversation. Better to just listen!

question: When should discharge planning ideally start in primary nursing?

options.A: When the patient complains about high hospital bills
options.B: Right upon the patient's admission to the unit
options.C: Only after the doctor signs the official discharge papers
options.D: On the exact morning the patient is scheduled to leave

explanation: Smart nursing! We start planning for home the very minute the patient walks through the door so nothing is rushed at the end.

question: Which physical finding is the classic hallmark of a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.B: Inability to walk due to paralysis of both legs
options.C: Severe lower abdominal swelling and tenderness
options.D: Continuous leakage of urine from the vaginal vault

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: To achieve a complete cure of the genetic mutation
options.B: To stop the natural progression of the disease entirely
options.C: To reverse the physical breakdown of body tissues
options.D: To maximize remaining function and quality of life

explanation: Because these genetic disorders are progressive and incurable, rehabilitation focuses on maintaining independence and quality of life rather than reversing the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h1)

question: What is the main difference between localized cancer treatments and systemic treatments?

options.A: Localized treatments are always surgical while systemic treatments are always oral
options.B: Systemic therapies only affect the specific organ where the tumor originally started
options.C: Systemic therapies travel through the bloodstream to reach cells throughout the body
options.D: Localized treatments cure cancer completely while systemic treatments only relieve pain

explanation: You've got this! Systemic treatments enter the bloodstream, which lets them reach cancer cells that might have traveled away from the main tumor site.

question: What do biological theories of aging primarily focus on?

options.A: Social interaction and community roles
options.B: Cellular damage and physical wear-and-tear
options.C: Retirement patterns and financial security
options.D: Emotional adjustment to loss

explanation: Biological theories look at physical changes, genetics, and cellular breakdown as the drivers of aging. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which behavior is a clear sign of medication non-adherence?

options.A: Asking the pharmacist about the cost of a new drug
options.B: Taking a morning pill one hour earlier than usual
options.C: Reporting a mild side effect to the attending nurse
options.D: Stopping a blood pressure pill because the patient feels better

explanation: Stopping medication simply because symptoms disappear shows a lack of adherence to the long-term treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to catch tummy (GI) warning signs early?

options.A: It completely removes the need to give IV fluids
options.B: It means nurses can skip doing physical tummy checks
options.C: It stops things like severe bleeding or a burst gut from getting worse fast
options.D: It makes sure the patient will never need surgery

explanation: Spotting warning signs early lets your healthcare team step in before life-threatening emergencies like heavy bleeding or bowel perforation happen.

question: What role do oral cholera vaccines play during an active outbreak?

options.A: Kill the bacteria inside contaminated river water sources
options.B: Provide short-term additional protection alongside water sanitation
options.C: Cure patients who already have severe rice-water diarrhea
options.D: Permanently immunize a population for the rest of their lives

explanation: Vaccines give a helpful shield during outbreaks, but they work best alongside clean water and good hygiene habits.

question: What is the main difference between a teaching method and a teaching technique in the classroom?

options.A: A technique is decided by the school board while a method is chosen by the student

options.D: A technique is used only in the classroom while a method is used strictly at the bedside
